non_goals: Does not prove ZFC-1 => B; it proves the HoTT side of the ruled reading: A with univalence makes B, dropping either stops it. That the same act A works on both sides is an accepted reading, not a theorem.
That A (the ready-made collection) is the defendant is the research sponsor's ruling D4-2 of 2026-10-15, not a theorem; the theorem is symmetric between the two causes.
Uses higher inductive types (Eilenberg-MacLane spaces); the local-global looping principle and the level of univalent universes of n-types are standard HoTT results (not claimed as original).

C-430: for every collection (codes with the members they name): (1) univalent and every height handed over at once (AllHeights) give no finite h-level, so the questioning program of C-77 is never for every judge; (2) univalent with member heights bounded by k gives h-level k+1, so the questioning halts; (3) if code sameness is a fact (codes form a set) the questioning stops at question 1; (4) read backwards: never needs unbounded heights (when univalent) and non-fact sameness; witnesses: (5a) the universe meets both and never stops (C-75/C-78 re-derived through (1), kernel runs fuel 1000); (5b) the gathering of the (1+n)-types is univalent and bounded and stops exactly at question 1+n; (5c) the numbered Eilenberg-MacLane collection (codes N, members EM Z (1+n)) has every height but fact sameness, stops at question 1 and is not univalent; (6) the paired collection (codes Type x Bool) has every height, is not univalent, and never stops, so (3) needs fact sameness, not mere failure of univalence.
